claims.text: A factory (broad sense used here) is a method or object whose job is to create objects, so the code that uses them never names the concrete class.

At stage-2 ShippingFeeFactory is a static class; static ForKind(string kind) returns ShippingFee: "standard" -> new StandardShipping(), "express" -> new ExpressShipping(), "pickup" -> new PickUpInStore(), anything else throws ArgumentException("unknown shipping kind: {kind}").
A C# switch expression evaluates its arms in text order and returns the result of the first arm whose pattern matches; the discard pattern _ matches any value.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: switch expression (evaluation order, discard pattern)

claims.text: A static method is called on the class name (ShippingFeeFactory.ForKind(...)) without creating an instance of the class.
claims.source_hint: C# programming guide: static classes and static class members

claims.text: At stage-2 the only callers of ShippingFeeFactory.ForKind are the tests in ShippingFeeFactoryTests (SamplesTests.cs); "same_day" is currently refused (test AnUnknownKindIsRefused).

ShippingFeeIfElseChain.ForOrder both recognises the kind string and computes the fee in each branch (standard: 0 from 2,000,000 else 30,000; express 60,000; pickup 0); StandardShipping holds the free-from-2,000,000 rule.

NotificationSender takes IServiceScopeFactory scopeFactory as a constructor parameter; each round SendDueAsync calls scopeFactory.CreateScope() and resolves NotificationQueue and IEmailSender from scope.ServiceProvider; the NotificationQueue it gets holds that round's fresh DonHangDbContext.
IServiceScopeFactory is registered by the framework itself when the host builder is created; app code does not register it. Đơn Hàng stage-2 has no registration of it.
claims.source_hint: dotnet docs: dependency-injection/service-registration.md, framework-registered services table; git grep IServiceScopeFactory @ stage-2

claims.text: IServiceScopeFactory.CreateScope returns a new IServiceScope each time it is called.
claims.source_hint: API reference: IServiceScopeFactory.CreateScope; dotnet docs dependency-injection/service-lifetimes.md

claims.text: In Đơn Hàng the DI container's registrations are all made once, at startup; none of them reads a customer's kind string such as "express" or registers a ShippingFee.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: Program.cs, ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs (no ShippingFee registration)

claims.text: Try it: adding SameDayShipping : ShippingFee (ForOrder returns 80_000) and the line "same_day" => new SameDayShipping() to ForKind, then dotnet test samples/DonHang.Samples.Tests --filter ShippingFeeFactoryTests: Failed!, 1 failed (AnUnknownKindIsRefused), 1 passed.

claims.text: A factory does not remove the branch on the kind; it moves it to one place whose only job is to pick a class, while fee rules stay in the subclasses.
With a factory, a new shipping kind costs one new subclass plus one new factory line; CheckoutTotal, existing fee classes and callers that get their fee from ForKind stay unchanged.

A DI container does not replace an application's own factory when the class to create depends on a value that arrives later (a customer's choice); the framework itself hands out factories such as IServiceScopeFactory.
